name: From 1 to Infinity
description: Vadim wanted to understand the infinite sequence of digits that consists of the positive integers written consecutively from $$$1$$$ to infinity. That is, this sequence looks like $$$123456789101112131415 \ldots$$$ To avoid looking into infinity, Vadim cut this sequence at the $$$k$$$-th digit and discarded everything after it. Thus, exactly $$$k$$$ digits remained in the sequence. Help him find the sum of the digits in the remaining sequence.
input_specification: Each test consists of several test cases. The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ $$$(1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^4)$$$ — the number of test cases. The following lines describe the test cases. In a single line of each test case, there is an integer $$$k$$$ — the number of digits in the remaining sequence $$$(1 \le k \le 10^{15})$$$.
output_specification: For each given $$$k$$$, output the sum of the digits in the sequence of length $$$k$$$.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2132D — From 1 to Infinity [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
